This one was tricky. The shapes in the Swap / Next area are whole images, but the shapes on the grid are made of individual cells.

Furthermore, to reduce CSS size I'm not using z-index. Cells that are to the right or below cover up bottom right edges of other cells. This is a problem when placing whole shapes into the grid because it will want to cover some cell sides and obscure others, but since it starts off to the right, and below the top area they obscure all cells. I could have had accepted a momentary glitch that would appear briefly during animation, but since I still have CSS space I went ahead and created correct visuals.

When a piece will be swapped the Swap shape area contains 3 shapes: The current shape in swap, initially visible then vanishes at the beginning of animation, The shape that will be entering swap from the grid initially invisible but fades in, and the shape that will animate from Swap onto the grid, which is invisible initially and appears only while animating. The secondary swap shape is used for animation to utilize the immediate on/off of visibility when animation stops (must disappear at end of animation), I may be able to tweak things to remove the additional shape, but it's only one extra image in the post when swapping a piece, and would not reduce CSS length (which is a primary concern).

The swapping shape is drawn above the grid, so when it reaches its destination it is hovering above the grid. The cells at the destination area depicting the swapped shape are initially invisible, then appear at the end of animation hovering above the grid, in the same place as the whole swapped shape. These cells render overlaps correctly as they fall into the grid.

The cells of the shape being swapped can't easily be made to animate into the Swap area. This is because they are relative posititoned, and would require between 30 to 200 different CSS rules to account for every position on the grid animating to the swap area. The shape entering the swap area thus fades out.

Shapes in the swap area have different offsets to center them. They could all just be left justified but it doesn't look as nice, IMO. This means that there are different animation rules depending on the swap shape's width.

The existing timing delay rules which allow temporal composition are reused to time the animations and can now be applied to the glowing drop guide. Previously the grid could contain 7 frames of monochrome animation (each cell only being one color or transparent), but now the grid can contain 7 frames of full color, since the falling cells can overwrite prior cells with a different color. This will be useful for non-stacking game mechanics.

This update breaks others because it moves the grid down by one cell to allow the hovering swap piece to be fully in view.
